summary: Multi-dimensional maximum load a vehicle can carry. Cumulative onboard load must never exceed capacity on any dimension at any point along the route.
range: Array of non-negative integers, one value per load dimension (e.g. [weight, volume, pallets]). No fixed upper bound in the spec.
constraints: Dimension count must stay consistent with jobs[].delivery, jobs[].pickup, and shipments[].amount.
businessRules: Hard constraint: for every dimension d, running onboard load <= capacity[d] at every step of the route.
Pickups increase load mid-route, so a load that is feasible at the depot can still breach capacity between a pickup and its delivery.
When violated, the offending task is placed in result.unassigned[] with a capacity reason; the solve still returns HTTP 200 and result.code == 0.

capacity defines: capacity attribute is used to define multidimensional capacities of the vehicle. It is recommended to keep the dimensions of capacity consistent with the dimensions provided in quantity related att…
Each element in capacity must be valid and consistent with related fields.
Must stay consistent with: jobs.delivery, jobs.pickup, shipments.amount. Changes here may require validation of those fields.
Rule: Capacity dimensions must match across jobs, shipments, and vehicles.
Rule: Higher priority jobs are serviced first; ties break by job ID order.
Optional field. Omitting uses solver's default behavior (no penalty).
validationRules: Inconsistent dimension lengths across capacity/delivery/pickup/amount -> 400 input validation failed.
Negative capacity value -> 400 input validation failed.
testingGuidance: Positive: capacity [100] with a single delivery [40] -> onboard load <= 100 at every step.
Boundary: demand exactly equal to capacity (delivery [50] on capacity [50]) fits.
Multi-dimension: capacity [10,100] with all deliveries/pickups/amounts 2-D and within both bounds -> accepted.
Negative-validation: dimension mismatch (capacity [10,100] but a job delivery [5]) -> 400.
Negative-infeasible: a single job whose delivery exceeds every vehicle's capacity -> in result.unassigned (capacity reason), still HTTP 200, result.code 0.
Negative-infeasible: capacity [10,100] with deliveries [2,60]+[2,50] breaches VOLUME (110>100) though weight (4<=10) is fine -> second job unassigned by volume.
Negative-infeasible: N jobs each delivery [1] on capacity [N] all fit; the (N+1)th on the same route breaches -> unassigned.
Interaction: zero-quantity demand is always capacity-feasible (a weightless stop).
Interaction: Negative: capacity [10,100] but a job delivery [5] (1 dim vs 2) -> HTTP 400 input validation failed.
Interaction: Positive: capacity [10,100] with all deliveries/pickups/amounts 2-dimensional -> accepted.
Interaction: Consistency: alternative_capacities with different dimension than primary capacity -> HTTP 400.
Interaction: Consistency: min_stop_load [20,30] but capacity [10,100] only -> dimension mismatch HTTP 400.
Interaction: Combination: tight capacity + one high-priority + one low-priority job competing for the last slot -> high-priority assigned, low-priority unassigned.
Interaction: Combination: high-priority job whose only skill is unavailable on any vehicle -> still unassigned despite priority.
Interaction: Interaction: two jobs with equal priority; one has outsourcing_cost 100, other 50 -> cost-based job assigned first.
